clue.text: A blaze — nothing breeds on the Camargue

definitions.note: the definition is a description, the bird that breeds there, rather than a verb

parts.note: read as one word, ablaze means on fire, flaming
nothing is zero, the round letter O

explanation.surface: A fire in which nothing survives sweeps across the marshes of southern France.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'A blaze' as 'ablaze', giving FLAMING. The Camargue is the Rhone delta wetland in southern France, famous for its colonies of pink wading birds.
explanation.definitionFit: The Camargue is the chief European nesting ground of the greater pink wading bird, so it is described by where it breeds.

clue.text: Tomorrow such a girl will be useful in the office

definitions.meaning: the day after Thursday, so tomorrow when today is Thursday

definitions.text: such a girl will be useful in the office
definitions.meaning: a Girl ... is an all-purpose office assistant

explanation.definitionFit: It is the weekday after Thursday, and an indispensable office helper is a Girl named after Crusoe's servant Man Friday.

clue.text: Jauntily holding one lira up to the end of the holiday

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the combined letters are read from bottom to top
holding means the currency word keeps the numeral inside it

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: the end of means take the last letter of holiday

explanation.surface: Someone carefree keeps a single lira in their pocket until the holiday is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' puts I inside LIRA to give LIRIA; 'up' turns it to AIRIL, and Y ends holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting airily means acting in a light, carefree manner, as jauntily does.

clue.text: Scandinavian halves of riding-switch

indicators.note: halves of tells us to split riding into its two three-letter parts
switch means those two halves change places

explanation.surface: Northern Europeans use part of a riding crop.
explanation.walkthrough: RID and ING swap places. 'Riding-switch' looks like a single noun, a horse whip, but 'switch' is the instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a common Swedish and Norwegian woman's name, as with the actress Bergman, so it fits a Scandinavian.

clue.text: Bring down the goose to a chorus of Boos?

definitions.text: Bring down the goose to a chorus of Boos?

parts.words: Bring down the goose to a chorus of Boos?
parts.note: shooting a goose is literally to bag a bird, and in theatre slang the bird is the hissing of an audience

explanation.surface: A hunter who shoots a goose is jeered by onlookers.
explanation.walkthrough: In British theatre slang, an actor who is hissed or booed 'gets the bird', from the hissing of geese.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to be booed or hissed off, and literally describes catching a fowl.

clue.text: Unruly coster's armed guard

indicators.note: unruly means disorderly, so the letters of the word beside it are put out of order

parts.note: the possessive 's is no letter, leaving the word coster to rearrange

explanation.surface: A rowdy street trader's protection is an armed bodyguard.
explanation.walkthrough: A coster (costermonger) is a British street seller of fruit and vegetables; 'Unruly' rearranges COSTER.
explanation.definitionFit: An escort is a guard, often armed, who travels with a person or convoy for protection.

clue.text: Coming in to cheat people and yet paying for their drinks

indicators.note: coming in to means the joining word enters the swindle word

parts.note: to sting is slang for to swindle or overcharge people

explanation.surface: A con man who fleeces people yet still buys them a round.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'stand' someone a drink is British for buying it for them; 'yet' links.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand a round is to treat others to drinks, so someone treating companions is doing this.

clue.text: Not what you'd call one who disregards orders

definitions.text: Not what you'd call one who disregards orders

parts.words: Not what you'd call one who disregards orders
parts.note: the description of someone who ignores commands is negated, so the word wanted means its opposite

explanation.surface: A comment that a rule-breaker hardly deserves a good reputation.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone compliant does as instructed, the opposite of a person who ignores commands.

clue.text: Adopt a menacing stance when Hare breaks into shaky tent

indicators.note: into means one set of letters is put inside the other
shaky means unsteady, so the letters of tent are jumbled
breaks means the letters of hare are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A hare bursts into a wobbly tent, alarming the campers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaks' turns HARE into HREA, 'shaky' turns TENT into TTEN, and 'into' puts HREA inside after the first T.
explanation.definitionFit: To menace someone is to warn them of harm, which is what posing aggressively does.

clue.text: How the canal system can get to the roots of the problem?

definitions.text: How the canal system can get to the roots of the problem?

parts.words: How the canal system can get to the roots of the problem?
parts.note: the figurative phrase about tackling a problem's causes is read literally, as channels carrying water to the roots of crops

explanation.surface: A question about how an organisation can tackle the underlying causes of its trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get to the roots of the problem' sounds like investigation; literally it is water reaching plant roots through canals, as in a dry farming region.
explanation.definitionFit: Supplying land with water through a network of channels is the farming practice described.

clue.text: Rush a professional course

definitions.meaning: to rush is to hurtle along out of control
one's working life followed through a profession

explanation.definitionFit: To hurtle headlong is to speed wildly, and a lifelong working path in one's profession carries the same name.

clue.text: Okay, so nobody's left

definitions.meaning: read as everyone present on the right-hand side, none on the left

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means satisfactory, and split as two words it says every one is on the right, with no one on the left.

clue.text: Mysterious Drood with a lady

parts.note: Dickens left unfinished The Mystery of Edwin Drood, so the mysterious Drood is Edwin

explanation.surface: The title character of Dickens's last mystery is paired with a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mystery of Edwin Drood is Charles Dickens's unfinished final novel; add A to his first name for a woman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a woman's given name, the feminine form of a man's name, so it can stand for a lady.

clue.text: Coming to a railway station without moving

definitions.text: Coming to a railway station without moving

parts.words: Coming to a railway station without moving
parts.note: coming to a station sounds like a journey, but the words describe a stopped train

explanation.surface: A train pulls into a station and halts.
explanation.walkthrough: A train arriving at a station comes to rest there, so the adjective formed on station describes it.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means not moving, and a train that has come into a station has stopped.

clue.text: Lack of indulgence sometimes associated with fast people

definitions.text: Lack of indulgence sometimes associated with fast people

parts.words: Lack of indulgence sometimes associated with fast people
parts.note: fast people seems to mean racy pleasure-seekers, but it means people who are fasting and so go without

explanation.surface: Self-denial is paradoxically linked to people who live wildly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast people' suggests a racy set who would never deny themselves; read it as people keeping a fast, who refrain from food.
explanation.definitionFit: Refraining from food, drink or pleasure is self-denial, the habit of those who keep a fast.

clue.text: Is Fido's initial energy turned to bone?

definitions.text: Is Fido's initial energy turned to bone?

indicators.note: turned means the letters are turned about into a new order

parts.note: here the s of the possessive counts as a letter

indicators.note: initial means take the first letter of energy

explanation.surface: A dog's early vigour is spent on chewing a bone, or has it hardened?
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' rearranges IS FIDOS E. Fido is the stock name for a dog, which fits the bone in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Tissue that has hardened into bone has calcified, which is what turned to bone means.

clue.text: Motor empire making a meal of making complaints

parts.note: BL is British Leyland, the former UK car-making conglomerate
making a meal of food is eating it

explanation.surface: A car firm makes a fuss over its troubles.
explanation.walkthrough: British Leyland, BL, was the giant state-backed British car maker of the 1970s. 'Making a meal of' sounds like making a fuss, but is read literally.
explanation.definitionFit: Bleating means whining or moaning, as complaining people do.

clue.text: Can such irritability be felt by those at the centre of things?

definitions.text: Can such irritability be felt by those at the centre of things?

parts.words: Can such irritability be felt by those at the centre of things?
parts.note: the word for nervy irritability is built on the rim of things, so those in the middle should be free of it

explanation.surface: Asks whether people at the heart of events can feel on edge.
explanation.walkthrough: Being nervy is being 'on edge', and the question asks if people at the centre, far from the edge, could feel it.
explanation.definitionFit: Nervy irritability means being on edge, tense and jumpy.

clue.text: Holding together Polish union

definitions.meaning: the trade union led by Lech Walesa in Poland in the 1980s

explanation.definitionFit: Unity of purpose among a group is one sense, and Solidarnosc, the Gdansk-born free trade union, is the other.

clue.text: Dexterous command to 11 in France

definitions.meaning: 11-across gives right, and a French instruction to turn to the right is a droite

explanation.definitionFit: Skilful with the hands is one sense, and read as French it is an order to go towards the right.

clue.text: Joke about nail makes one open-mouthed

indicators.note: about means the joke word goes around the nail word

parts.note: a gag is a joke
a pin is a small nail

explanation.surface: A gag about a nail leaves a listener astonished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts PIN inside GAG.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaping means staring with the mouth wide, as someone astonished does.

clue.text: Home Counties shown up in this scholastic essay

indicators.note: in means the reversed letters go inside this
in a down clue, shown up means the letters are read upwards, back to front

parts.note: the Home Counties around London are in the South East, SE

explanation.surface: London's surrounding counties are featured in an academic paper.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the English counties surrounding London, in the South East. 'shown up' turns SE to ES, and 'in' puts it inside THIS.
explanation.definitionFit: A dissertation written for a university degree is an extended academic essay.

clue.text: No upright type, it may be necessary to emphasise

definitions.text: No upright type, it may be necessary to emphasise

parts.words: No upright type, it may be necessary to emphasise
parts.note: an upright type sounds like an honest person, but here type is printing lettering, and the sloping kind is used for emphasis

explanation.surface: A shady character might be needed to make a point forcefully.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upright type' suggests a person of good character; in printing, the sloping typeface is the one that is not upright and is used for emphasis.
explanation.definitionFit: The sloping typeface, as opposed to upright roman, is used in print to stress words.

clue.text: Riotous old bat ch, but won't get into hot water

indicators.note: riotous means wild and disorderly, so the letters that follow are rearranged

explanation.surface: A wild old woman exclaims, yet manages to stay out of trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: The page's 'oh' is an OCR slip for 'ch'; 'Riotous' rearranges OLD BAT CH. 'Get into hot water' sounds like getting into trouble, but means a literal bath.
explanation.definitionFit: A plunge into unheated water is the opposite of soaking in a hot tub, so it never involves hot water.

clue.text: Part of his alibi demolished though classically in the same place

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters lying inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A suspect's alibi is torn apart, citing the same source over and over.
explanation.walkthrough: The Latin term is used in footnotes to refer back to a source just cited; 'classically' flags it as Latin.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the Latin word meaning in that very place, used in references to repeat a citation.

clue.text: Weeps about a pound overweight initially; they should have been counted!

indicators.note: about means going around, so the weeping word wraps the other pieces

parts.note: weeps means cries
L, from libra, is the abbreviation for a pound

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of overweight

explanation.surface: Someone tearful at being a pound heavy realises they should have watched their diet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts A, L and O inside CRIES. The definition works with the whole surface: units of food energy are what a dieter counts.
explanation.definitionFit: Dieters keep tally of the energy units in their food, so these are what an overweight person should have counted.

clue.text: Gradually take in implications of the abstract

definitions.meaning: to absorb and come to understand an idea over time
an abstract is a summary of a longer text

explanation.definitionFit: To absorb and mull over information is one sense, and a condensed summary or compilation is the noun sense.

clue.text: How a 10 in rep is gradually advanced?

definitions.text: How a 10 in rep is gradually advanced?

parts.words: How a 10 in rep is gradually advanced?
parts.note: 10 is a professional course, and in repertory theatre an actor's progress happens on the boards

explanation.surface: A question about how an actor's working life in repertory theatre moves forward.
explanation.walkthrough: 10-across is CAREER; 'rep' is repertory theatre, a touring or resident company. 'Gradually' gives the phrase's meaning, and an actor's progress literally comes on theatre platforms.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means step by step, and stage also names a theatre's platform where actors work.
